descriptionMarkdown:
Use Chapter 18’s Availability and provenance rules. Success normally grants a mission loan or support, not personal 
ownership. Agree the chassis, listed weapons, supplies, crew arrangements, route and recovery conditions. Vehicles 
are not class starting equipment unless explicitly granted by the GM.
Civilian transport fits early missions; armed scouts and carriers require credible faction support. Tanks and alien grav-
tanks are substantial assets, even for experienced warbands. Low-level crews can be assigned one, but need a reason 
it cannot solve every obstacle. Captured vehicles still require access, supplies, maintenance and a safe destination; 
possessing one does not make its use lawful or consequence-free.
Each vehicle has two modification slots. Fit one upgrade per slot and never duplicate it. Fitting or replacing one takes 
four hours in a suitable workshop with tools. Undamaged upgrades can be recovered. Built-in traits use no slots. 
Personal armour or weapon upgrades do not apply to hulls or mounts unless explicitly permitted.
Upgrade Availability Effect
Reinforced plating Rare
Add 20 maximum and current HP when fitted. Speed −10 ft, minimum 
10 ft. Removal removes 20 current HP, minimum 1. No AC or DT 
increase.
Smoke launchers Controlled
Two uses per mission. Driver or gunner action creates stationary smoke in a 
20-ft radius centred on the vehicle until the start of that operator’s next turn. 
Attacks through it have disadvantage; no protection against area effects.
Auspex survey suite Scarce
A crew member scanning as an action gains advantage on one Perception or 
Survival check for routes, obstacles or ambushes within 300 ft. Does not see 
through solid barriers.
Recovery winch Controlled
At rest, an operator’s action pulls an unsecured or willing object up to cargo 
capacity by 10 ft. With a sound anchor, ten minutes frees the vehicle from 
ordinary mud or a shallow ditch.
All-terrain running gear Scarce Wheeled or tracked chassis ignores difficult terrain from mud, loose rubble 
and shallow debris; not walls, deep water or impassable slopes.
Sealed compartment Rare Enclosed chassis gains Sealed and one hour of internal air. Cannot fit to 
exposed bikes or open-topped vehicles.
Ogryn accommodation Controlled
Convert one suitable crew station for an Ogryn OR reinforce suitable 
passenger space so an Ogryn uses two spaces instead of three. Choose one 
version; no duplicates. Chassis must have enough physical room.
Spare-parts locker Scarce
Includes two repair kits. Once per mission reroll one failed field-repair check, 
using the new result. Expended kits need replacement; locker remains 
reusable.
Weapon swaps need GM approval, the new weapon’s Availability, a compatible mount and four workshop hours. A 
swap replaces a mount’s weapon; it does not add a weapon or crew station. An integral bike or walker weapon cannot 
be removed and wielded as an ordinary personal firearm.
Travel times follow the route and the vehicle’s fictional capabilities, not a conversion of tactical Speed into miles per 
hour. A compact chase, a breakdown and a choice of route are usually more useful than tracking fuel for every mile.
Vehicle Profiles
